A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MallowsPO paper, with 33 pages and complete Appendices A–G. Full text and rendered-page comparisons establish that differences are confined to the acknowledgement and first-page arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v4 reports original synthetic-bandit and language-model experiments in Section 5, with additional evaluations, hyperparameter comparisons, and qualitative results in Appendix F.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix F, including the model comparisons in Table 1.

M1.justification: The MallowsPO-θ and MallowsPO-ϕ objectives, entropy-based dispersion estimator, computational approximations, and adaptations to IPO and SimPO are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic bandit, IMDB, Anthropic-HH, UltraFeedback, SHP, H4 Stack Exchange, and Alpaca Eval V2 coverage, including the same out-of-distribution evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout: DPO remains the principal baseline, and Table 1 retains the same IPO and SimPO comparisons with their Mallows-enhanced counterparts.

E3.justification: Sections 5 and Appendices E–F report identical model configurations, training settings, hyperparameter grids, evaluation metrics, and GPT-4/ArmoRM judging procedures.

E4.justification: Dispersion-estimator validation, reward-collapse analysis, generalization tests, the β/learning-rate analysis in Appendix F.2, and qualitative examples in Figures 15–20 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the ten-random-seed comparison in Section 5.5, five-run reporting for Figure 14, and the same standard-deviation and error-bar reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plots, and qualitative examples match. For example, Table 1 reports the same LC win rates of 42.55% for DPO and 43.10% for MallowsPO; Appendix F's results are also identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, propositions, theorems, and derivations in Sections 3–4 and Appendices B–D are unchanged, including the generalized ΨPO connection.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about incorporating preference dispersion, generalizing DPO, improving benchmark performance, and compatibility with other preference-optimization methods.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and unresolved questions about mechanisms, β selection, and dispersion estimation are unchanged. Appendix G retains the same curriculum-learning and personalized-alignment discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix E's implementation details, optimizers, learning rates, batch sizes, and evaluation instructions are identical. Code-access information and link destinations are also unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to Bradley–Terry models and existing preference-optimization methods are identical.

P1.justification: On page 11, v5 adds Haoxian Chen alongside Hanyang Zhao and Wenpin Tang as supported by NSF grant DMS-2206038. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; scientific prose and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgement edit causes local line rewrapping, and the first-page arXiv stamp changes. All scientific figures, tables, captions, and placements remain identical, including those in the appendices.

improvement.justification: v5 adds a funding attribution and updates the arXiv stamp, without changing scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information, or substantive presentation. These administrative edits do not establish a meaningful change in overall paper quality.
